bearCase: Calendar 2026 capex near $190B creates a long cash-conversion lag or structurally lower returns.
Microsoft Cloud gross margin falls below the 64% Q4 guide and does not stabilize in FY2027.
Headline RPO growth remains concentrated in OpenAI commitments and does not broaden.
Copilot adoption grows without adequate ARPU or incremental margin.
The apparent GAAP P/E discount is partly an artifact of volatile OpenAI investment accounting.
bullCase: Azure maintains roughly 40% constant-currency growth while capacity comes online.
Copilot paid seats and ARPU accelerate through Microsoft's enterprise distribution.
Non-OpenAI RPO converts into durable revenue and cash flow.
Operating leverage and infrastructure efficiency offset depreciation and AI usage costs.
AI capex proves predominantly growth investment rather than a permanent maintenance burden.
result.decisionHinge: AI capital spending must convert into durable Azure and Copilot growth, stable cloud margins, and recovering free cash flow.
missingEvidence: A reproducible, same-date distribution of current sell-side ratings and price targets.
A direct Morningstar update after FY2026 Q3; the available item is dated 2026-01-22.
A complete company split of maintenance versus growth capex across GPUs, CPUs, buildings, land, and infrastructure.
FY2026 Q4, full-year FY2026, and formal FY2027 results, which are scheduled for 2026-07-29.
A peer valuation set normalized for accounting, growth, capex, stock compensation, and net cash.
